title: Writing practice: Retells, notes, claims, and explanations
description: Eight writing tasks across school subjects: retell a story, explain with numbers, support a claim with data, and write a welcome message to a new student.

stimuli.title: Read: Ming's Paper Boat
paragraphs: Ming's class had a paper boat contest on Friday. Each student made a boat from paper and tape, and the boat had to float across a water tray.
Ming folded his boat carefully. But when he set it in the water, the paper soaked up the water and the boat sank. Ming felt discouraged.

His friend Rosa said, “Paper takes in water. Try something waxy.” Ming rubbed a candle stub over a new paper boat and set it in the tray. This time, the boat floated all the way across. Ming smiled and thanked Rosa.

stimuli.title: Bike rental prices
stimuli.caption: Two shops rent bicycles. Each shop charges a starting fee once, plus a price for each hour.

stimuli.title: Spoons in hot soup
stimuli.caption: Two spoons of the same size, one metal and one wood, were put in the same pot of hot soup. A student carefully touched each handle every minute and wrote down when it first felt warm. Heat moves from warmer things to cooler things. Metal lets heat move through it faster than wood does.
columns: Time until the handle felt warm

stimuli.title: Two proposals for the town's fund
stimuli.caption: The town council has $45,000 to spend and can pay for only one project. The table gives facts about each proposal.
columns: Proposal B: Repair the Community Pool
rows: About 600 riders each weekday, including workers and students
About 150 swimmers each day during the 3 summer months, and about 400 children in free swim lessons each year
Connects the east side of town to the hospital and two schools
The only public pool in town; it gives children a place to learn to swim; the pool is closed the rest of the year
East-side residents keep traveling 90 minutes by two buses
The pool stays closed because of a leak, and the nearest pool is in another town

stimuli.title: Our morning schedule
stimuli.caption: This is what your class does each morning.
rows: Attendance and morning work at our desks
Reading groups in three parts of the room

stimuli.title: Read: The Night Ferry
paragraphs: Imani had never been on the night ferry alone. Her grandmother had fallen asleep on the bench, and there were only a few other passengers on the dim lower deck. When the engine coughed and went silent, the lights flickered, and the deck tilted slightly in the dark. Imani's hands were shaking, and her heart pounded.

A small boy near the rail began to cry. Imani wanted to run to her grandmother, but instead she took a deep breath, walked to the boy, and knelt beside him. “Look,” she said softly, pointing at the stars, “we can count them until the engine starts again.”
By the time the crew restarted the motor, the boy had counted to forty-one, and Imani realized her hands had stopped shaking.

stimuli.title: Keeping a hot drink warm
stimuli.caption: Four identical cups were filled with water at 80°C. Three cups were wrapped in different covers, and one cup was left uncovered. After 20 minutes, the water temperature in each cup was measured.

stimuli.title: Read: The Erie Canal
paragraphs: Before 1825, goods in the northeastern United States traveled mostly by wagon on rough roads. Moving one ton of freight from Buffalo, on Lake Erie, to New York City cost about $100, and the trip was slow.
In 1825, workers finished the Erie Canal, a waterway about 363 miles long. It connected the Hudson River to Lake Erie, so boats could carry goods between the Great Lakes and the Atlantic coast.

After the canal opened, shipping one ton of freight cost less than $10. Farmers near the Great Lakes could sell their grain in distant markets, and factories in the East could send their products west. Towns along the canal, such as Rochester and Buffalo, grew quickly as workers, families, and merchants moved there.

items.stem: Your classmate Ayo was absent on Friday. Retell what happened to Ming in the order it happened, so that Ayo understands the story.

checklist: I told the events in the order they happened.
I used time words such as first, then, after that, and in the end.
I used past-tense verbs such as sank, said, and floated.
I told how Ming solved his problem.
exemplar: Retells the main events in sequence: the first boat sinks, Rosa gives advice, the waxed boat floats
Shows cause and effect in the writer's own words (the paper soaked up water, so the boat sank; the wax helped)
Uses sequence words and past-tense verbs consistently
Retells in own words rather than copying whole sentences from the text

support.clue: Look for the problem first, then the advice Rosa gives, then what happens to the second boat. Notice the order of the three paragraphs.
support.frame: First, Ming ______. However, ______. Then Rosa ______. After that, Ming ______. In the end, ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different story. “First, Kofi planted a seed in a cup. After a week, nothing grew because the cup was in a dark closet. Then his aunt told him to move it to a window. After that, Kofi watered it every day. In the end, a green sprout appeared.” Notice the order words and the problem, the advice, and the result. Now retell Ming's story the same way.

facts: Paper absorbs water and can sink when it is soaked.
Wax repels water, so a waxed paper surface soaks up less water.

items.stem: Maya wants to rent a bike for 4 hours. Explain how to find the total cost at each shop, and tell which shop costs less for 4 hours. Show your numbers.

checklist: I showed the calculation for Green Wheels, including the starting fee.
I showed the calculation for City Cycles.
I compared the two totals and named the cheaper shop.
I used words such as multiply, add, total, and because.
exemplar: Finds the Green Wheels total: $6 + 4 × $5 = $26, and the City Cycles total: 4 × $7 = $28
Explains each step in words (multiply the hourly price by 4, then add the starting fee)
Concludes that Green Wheels costs $2 less and states the comparison clearly
Uses mathematical vocabulary (total, starting fee, for each hour) and connectors accurately

support.clue: For each shop, read the caption again: what does the shop charge once, and what does it charge for every hour? Then think about how many hours Maya rents the bike.
support.frame: At Green Wheels, to find the cost for 4 hours, I ______. The total is ______. At City Cycles, ______. Therefore, ______ is cheaper because ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different problem. “A school store sells pencils for $2 each and notebooks for $3 each. To find the cost of 3 pencils and 2 notebooks, I multiply 2 by 3 to get 6 dollars for the pencils. Then I multiply 3 by 2 to get 6 dollars for the notebooks. The total is 6 + 6 = 12 dollars. A bundle of the same things costs $11, so the bundle costs less.” Notice that each step says what the numbers mean. Explain the bike shops the same way.

facts: Green Wheels total for 4 hours: 6 + 5 × 4 = 26 dollars.
City Cycles total for 4 hours: 7 × 4 = 28 dollars.
26 dollars is 2 dollars less than 28 dollars.

items.stem: Explain why the handle of the metal spoon felt warm sooner than the handle of the wooden spoon. Use the idea that heat moves from warmer things to cooler things.

checklist: I said which handle felt warm sooner and used numbers from the table.
I explained why, using the words heat, metal, and wood.
I used a cause-and-effect word such as because, so, or as a result.
exemplar: States the result with data: 2 minutes for the metal handle and 9 minutes for the wooden handle
Explains the cause: heat moves from the hot soup through the metal faster, so the metal handle warms sooner
Uses cause-and-effect connectors (because, so, as a result) correctly
Uses science vocabulary (heat, metal, wood, warm) accurately

support.clue: Compare the two times in the table. Then read the caption again: what does it say about how heat moves through metal and through wood?
support.frame: The ______ spoon’s handle felt warm sooner. It took ______ minutes, but the other handle took ______ minutes. This happened because ______. As a result, ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different topic. “The toy car rolled farther on the smooth floor than on the carpet. This happened because the rough carpet slows the car more than the smooth floor does. As a result, the car stopped sooner on the carpet.” Notice the result, the word because, and the result word. Explain the spoons the same way.

facts: Heat moves from warmer objects to cooler objects.
Metals conduct heat better than wood does, so heat moves through a metal spoon faster.
The times in the table are invented for this practice.
A rough surface slows a rolling object more than a smooth surface does (used in the mentor example only).

items.stem: Write a letter to the town council that argues which proposal the town should fund. Support your position with at least two details from the table, and respond to one reason someone might disagree.

checklist: I stated my position clearly near the beginning.
I used at least two details from the table as evidence.
I explained how each detail supports my position.
I wrote about a different opinion and explained why my position is still stronger.
I used formal language and connectors such as however, therefore, and in addition.
exemplar: States a clear position in an opening that addresses the council; either proposal can be defended with evidence

Selects relevant evidence from the table (for example 600 weekday riders compared with 150 summer swimmers and 400 children in swim lessons, or year-round use compared with the only public pool) and cites numbers accurately
Explains how each piece of evidence supports the position rather than only listing facts
Acknowledges a different view and answers it with concession language (although, however)
Uses formal register, organized paragraphs, and accurate connectors

support.clue: Compare the two columns row by row. Which facts show who benefits most, and for how many months of the year? Choose the facts that best fit your position.
support.frame: I am writing to recommend that the council fund ______. First, the table shows that ______. This matters because ______. In addition, ______. Some people may argue that ______. However, ______. For these reasons, ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different issue. “I recommend that the school buy new library books instead of a new scoreboard. First, the survey shows that 300 students use the library each week. This matters because books help everyone learn. Some people may argue that a scoreboard is exciting. However, it would be used only a few times a year. For these reasons, books are the better choice.” Notice the position, the evidence, the explanation, and the answer to disagreement. Do the same with the town's two proposals.

facts: The council has $45,000 and can fund only one project (given in the task).
Proposal A costs $42,000 and Proposal B costs $45,000 (given in the table).
Proposal A serves about 600 weekday riders; Proposal B serves about 150 swimmers a day for 3 months (given in the table).
Proposal B also serves about 400 children in free swim lessons each year, is the only public pool in town, and is closed for the rest of the year (given in the table).

items.stem: A new student will join your class tomorrow. Write a short welcome message that tells the new student what the class does in the morning and at what times.

checklist: I began with a welcome and ended politely.
I told at least three activities and their times.
I used time words and clear sentences.
exemplar: Uses a friendly welcome and closing suited to a message to a new classmate
Presents at least three activities with the correct times from the table
Uses time expressions (at, after, then) and present tense for routines
Language is polite, clear, and organized in the order of the day

support.clue: Read the table from top to bottom. Each row has a time and something the class does.
support.frame: Welcome to our class! Our morning starts at ______, when we ______. At ______, we ______. Then ______. I hope ______. Your classmate, ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different welcome. “Welcome to our swim club! At 4:00, we change and put our bags in the lockers. At 4:15, we warm up with stretches. At 5:00, we practice in small groups. Please bring a towel and a water bottle. See you soon, Sam.” Notice the welcome, the times and activities, and the friendly closing. Write your message the same way.

items.stem: Is Imani brave? Write a paragraph that states your claim and supports it with at least two details from the story. Explain how each detail proves your claim.

checklist: I stated a clear claim about Imani.
I used two details from the story as evidence.
I explained how each detail supports my claim.
I used a connecting word such as because, although, or for example.
exemplar: Takes a clear position and defines the idea (for example, acting calmly while still afraid)
Cites specific details from the text (her shaking hands, kneeling beside the boy, pointing at the stars)
Explains how each detail proves the claim rather than only retelling
Uses evidence phrases (for example, the story says) and contrast language (although, even though)
Organizes the paragraph as claim, evidence, reasoning, and closing sentence

support.clue: Find two places where the story shows Imani’s feelings and two places where it shows what she does. Decide what being brave means to you, then check whether the details fit.
support.frame: I think Imani is ______ because ______. For example, the story says that ______. This shows that ______. Another detail is ______. This proves that ______ because ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different character. “I believe Diego is generous because he shares even when he has little. For example, the story says he gave half of his lunch to a new student. This shows that he puts others first. Another detail is that he never asks for thanks. This proves he is generous because he gives without wanting a reward.” Notice the claim, the story detail, and the explanation after each detail. Use the same moves for Imani.

items.stem: A good insulator slows the movement of heat out of a drink. Write a scientific argument about which cover is the best insulator. State your claim, use data from the table as evidence, and explain your reasoning.

checklist: I made a claim that names one cover.
I used at least two numbers from the table as evidence.
I explained why the numbers support my claim.
I used science words such as insulator, heat, and temperature.
exemplar: Claim names the foam sleeve as the best insulator
Evidence cites specific data (66°C with the foam sleeve compared with 47°C with no cover, or temperature drops of 14°C and 33°C)
Reasoning explains that a smaller temperature drop means less heat escaped, so the material slows heat transfer better
Compares the best cover with at least one other cover
Uses accurate science vocabulary and a claim, evidence, reasoning organization

support.clue: Find the cover where the water stayed hottest. Compare its final temperature with the No cover row. Think: what does a smaller drop in temperature tell you about heat?
support.frame: My claim is that the ______ is the best insulator. The evidence is that the water in the cup with the ______ was ______°C after 20 minutes, but ______. This shows that ______ because ______. In contrast, ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different experiment. “My claim is that dark soil warms fastest. The evidence is that the dark soil reached 31°C, while the light soil reached only 26°C. This shows that dark soil takes in more sunlight because dark colors absorb more light. In contrast, the light soil reflected more of the light.” Notice the claim, the numbers, and the reason that links them. Write your argument about the cups the same way.

facts: An insulator slows the transfer of heat.
A smaller drop in temperature means that less heat left the cup.
Temperature drops: foam sleeve 14°C, wool sock 19°C, aluminum foil 28°C, no cover 33°C (80 minus the final temperature).
Dark surfaces absorb more sunlight than light surfaces.

items.stem: Explain how the Erie Canal changed the cost of shipping goods and how that change affected farmers and towns. Use a chain of causes and effects from the passage.

checklist: I explained what the canal changed about the cost of shipping.
I explained at least two effects on people or towns.
I used cause-and-effect words such as because, as a result, and led to.
I used details from the passage.
exemplar: Identifies the central change: shipping one ton fell from about $100 to less than $10
Builds a chain: cheaper shipping, then farmers and factories could sell farther away, then towns along the canal grew
Uses causal language (because, as a result, led to, so) accurately
Uses specific details from the passage (1825, Buffalo, Rochester, the Hudson River)
Orders the ideas so that each effect becomes the next cause

support.clue: Find the sentence that tells the cost before the canal and the sentence that tells the cost after. Then ask: what could farmers and factories do because of that change?
support.frame: Before the canal, ______. After the canal opened, ______. Because shipping became ______, farmers could ______. As a result, ______. This led to ______.
support.model: Mentor example about a different change. “Before the school bus route was added, many students walked two miles. After the route opened, the trip took less time. Because walking was no longer necessary, more students arrived on time. As a result, classes started with fewer interruptions. This led to better learning.” Notice how each effect becomes the next cause. Explain the canal's changes the same way.

facts: The Erie Canal opened in 1825.
The canal was about 363 miles long and connected the Hudson River to Lake Erie.
Shipping a ton of freight between Buffalo and New York City cost about $100 before the canal and less than $10 after it.
Towns along the canal, including Rochester and Buffalo, grew quickly after it opened.
